From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: POC trial planning + workload intake — Acme Health

Hi Jane —

Great to speak earlier. Quick recap of actions and next steps from our call so we have alignment going into the POC: 

1) Success criteria (owner: Acme) — you mentioned two primary goals:
   - Reduce inference cost per request by ~30% vs current hosted endpoint
   - Maintain median 95th percentile latency under 350ms for typical queries

2) Evaluation plan (owner: Acme + Redwood) — 2-week trial with representative traffic, Redwood will provide a test cluster and telemetry. We’ll run:
   - Week 1: functional validation with real samples (sanitized)
   - Week 2: performance soak under traffic profile we agree on

3) Workload intake (owner: Acme -> provide; Redwood -> validate) — items we need from you by EOD Thu (4/22):
   - Typical & peak RPS (average RPS and apparent burst behaviour)
   - Token length distribution (prompt / completion averages and 95th pct)
   - Concurrency targets (simultaneous requests)
   - Any tail/long-run batch jobs or nightly bursts
   - Example sample prompts (5–10) and representative completions

4) Timeline & resources — proposed start 5/3; Redwood SRE (Dylan) and Solutions Eng (Marissa) will own setup.

5) Logistics & compliance — send SOC2 questionnaire items to security@acmehealth or I can kick off our standard checklist if helpful.

Attachments: I’m attaching a quick success-criteria template and a network/profile CSV for the intake.

Can you confirm owners and whether the proposed start date works? Happy to jump on another 30m call if you want to walk through the intake fields.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Thanks Ben — and thanks everyone on the call yesterday. Quick reply with initial answers; Tom and I will follow up with CSVs by Thursday.

- Owners: I (Jane) will be the internal POC lead; Tom will provide the traffic metrics and coordinate infra changes.
- Start date: 5/3 works for us.
- Success criteria: agreed as above, plus we want to measure tokenization parity vs our current pipeline (same prompts, same stopping criteria).

Traffic notes (high-level):
- Average RPS: ~12 rps during peak business hours (UTC-7); baseline ~2 rps off-hours.
- Burst behaviour: spikes up to ~110 rps for ~20–30s during report runs and end-of-day churn; occasional longer bursts tied to scheduled jobs (~5–10 minutes).
- Typical token lengths: prompt avg 180 tokens (95th: 620), completion avg 60 tokens (95th: 220).
- Concurrency: typical concurrency 8–12, target soak test concurrency 40.

We’ll attach the CSV with per-minute RPS histograms and example prompts. Also attaching sample SLA requirements we run internally.

Best,
Jane
Jane Doe
Product Lead, AI Integrations
Acme Health
jane.doe@acmehealth.com

Thanks Jane — this is perfect and really helpful. A couple follow-ups so we can size the POC cluster and risk-profile the rollout: 

- For the 110 rps 20–30s bursts, is that usually a single origin (one IP/service) or fan-in from many clients? If single origin we can route through a scaled node; if many origins we’ll plan for ingress load-balancing.
- Do you have an SLO for 95th percentile latency (you mentioned 350ms target). Is that measured at the client-side or including network hop to our region?
- For tokenization parity: can you share the exact tokenizer/version you use (or sample tokenized output) so we can validate equivalent token counts?

Operational asks from our side (we can validate once we get CSVs):
- SSH/egress rules for our test agents (we’ll provide a limited set of IPs)
- Certificate or allowlist steps for your VPC if you plan private connectivity

Next steps (owners):
- Acme: send CSVs and sample prompts (by 4/22) — OWNER: Tom
- Redwood: validate intake and produce a POC config + estimated cost/cluster sizing (by 4/27) — OWNERS: Marissa/Dylan
- Schedule 30m kickoff for 5/3 — OWNER: Ben (will send calendar invite)

I’ll draft the kickoff invite and include required attendees. If you prefer we can do a short runbook review ahead of start date.

Cheers,
Ben
